This gives $-3-4i$, not $-3+4i$, so the check does not confirm the answer.

The final answer is wrong. The correct value is $1+2i$, not $-1+2i$.

The error is an arithmetic slip in the numerator expansion:

$$(-3+4i)(1-2i)=-3+6i+4i-8i^2=-3+10i+8=5+10i$$

The real part is $-3+8=5$, not $-5$. Dividing by 5 gives $1+2i$.

The alternative shortcut is also invalid. Flipping only the real part of $\frac{11}{5}-\frac{2}{5}i$ does not account for the change in the numerator. Since $(-3+4i)=(3+4i)-6$, we get

$$\frac{-3+4i}{1+2i}=\frac{3+4i}{1+2i}-\frac{6}{1+2i}=\left(\frac{11}{5}-\frac{2}{5}i\right)-\left(\frac{6}{5}-\frac{12}{5}i\right)=1+2i$$

This agrees with the direct computation. The value $-\frac{11}{5}-\frac{2}{5}i$ from the shortcut is not the correct quotient.
